text: It was once well said of a certain German book that it does not permit itself to be read, and in the same way there are some secrets which do not permit themselves to be told. <break time="0.8s" /> Many a man dies quietly in his bed with a secret still locked in his heart, unable to reveal the very mystery that has haunted his conscience for years. <break time="0.8s" /> Not long ago, one autumn evening, I sat at the large bow window of a coffee house in London, for I had been ill for several months and was only now recovering my strength. <break time="0.8s" /> Freed at last from the dull fog of illness, I was in one of those rare moods of heightened keenness, when the film seems to fall from the minds eye and every trifle offers calm delight. <break time="0.8s" /> For some time I amused myself by reading the advertisements in a newspaper, but at length my attention was drawn to the street outside, which was one of the principal thoroughfares of the city. <break time="0.8s" /> As darkness came on, the throng thickened every moment, and by the time the lamps were lit, two dense and continuous tides of people were rushing past the door. <break time="0.8s" /> I had never before been in a similar situation at such an hour, and the tumultuous sea of human heads filled me with a delicious novelty of emotion. <break time="0.8s" /> At first my observations took an abstract and general turn, but soon I descended to details, regarding with minute interest the innumerable varieties of figure, dress, air, gait, and expression.
